name: github
description: Work with GitHub repos, issues, and pull requests using the user's own token. Load for repo/issue/PR reads, searches, creating issues and comments.

content.inline:
## GitHub
Calls go through `v/ops/http/get` / `v/ops/http/post` against `https://api.github.com` with `bearerSecret: "s/GITHUB_TOKEN"` (a fine-grained or classic personal access token: Settings -> Developer settings -> Personal access tokens; grant only the repos and scopes the task needs). Send headers `Accept: application/vnd.github+json` and `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28`. Only the secret reference goes in the request; never the token.

Common calls:
- Whoami: `GET /user`
- Your repos: `GET /user/repos?per_page=100&sort=updated` (page via the `Link` header `rel="next"`)
- Repo issues: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues?state=open&per_page=100`
- One issue: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}`
- Create issue: `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues` body `{title, body?, labels?, assignees?}`
- Comment: `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/comments` body `{body}`
- Pull requests: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=open`
- Search: `GET /search/issues?q=<encoded>` (e.g. `repo:owner/name is:open is:issue`)
- File contents: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}` (base64 in `content`)

Rules:
- Check `status`; errors are `{message, documentation_url}`. 401 = bad/expired token; 403 with `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` = rate limited (wait for `X-RateLimit-Reset`); 404 on a private repo usually means the token was not granted it.
- Fine-grained tokens are scoped per repo. If a repo 404s, add it to the token.
- Use `search/issues` for cross-repo queries but sparingly; its rate limit is lower. URL-encode `q` with `v/ops/jvm/url-encode`.
